items.title: It turns out Jensen Huang is just as awful as the other tech overlords
items.content:
A few days ago, you were minding your own business, unconcerned about Jensen Huang or his penis. Perhaps you were still celebrating last week’s election results, and the mild improvement to civilization those results portended. When suddenly, out of nowhere, the name JENSEN HUANG was all over your internet, your nightly news, perhaps even your group text chains. Now you can’t stop hearing about this man, or about how he and his libido got trapped in a byzantine web of international intrigue that involves multitrillion-dollar companies, Silicon Valley, China, the president of the United States, and the growing scourge of artificial intelligence. Who is this Jensen Huang fella, and what exactly has he gotten America into?

Reader, fear not. I am a licensed journaltician, and I have a penis of my own. That makes me the most qualified man in America to answer all of your questions regarding this, the juiciest tech scandal since Lizzy Holmes tried to suck cancer patients’ blood using a busted Texas Instruments calculator. Let’s get to the tea.

Huang is a Taiwanese American Stanford grad who currently serves as CEO of Nvidia, a hardware company that has become one of the most valuable companies on the planet.

Article continues below this ad

Q: How did Nvidia get so big?Because it produces the chips that virtually every American AI company uses to power their now ubiquitous large language models. When the introduction of ChatGPT launched the AI boom a couple of years ago, it was Huang’s chips providing virtually all of the hardware underneath that technology’s infrastructure. As a result, the company’s stock price increased by orders of magnitude, growing Huang’s billions and making Nvidia itself worth trillions. Along the way, Huang got the familiar kid glove treatment from the tech press, who lavished the baron with photo shoots of him clad in his beloved leather jacket, and portraying him as a different breed of cat from all of the other Stanford grads.

Q: What made him different?Huang famously eschewed normal, snooty CEO practices in favor of having his employees email him directly. Specifically, he has them outline the “Top 5” things they’re working on at any given moment, which gives him a clearer idea of what’s happening at Nvidia, rather than just relying on a few yes-men to feed him daily rations of bulls—t. Tesla CEO Elon Musk would later steal the “five things” format as a means of having his DOGE goons hollow out the federal government.

Article continues below this ad

Why yes.

Q: OK, enough of the background stuff. Get to the sexy business.Hold up, I still have a bit more pre-explaining to do.

I deserved that. Now, the American AI market is a tangle of self-dealing that, as with all financial boondoggles, is deliberately opaque. The less regular folks understand about what these entities are doing, the more they can get away with. But Huang apparently wasn’t satisfied with his company merely dominating the American AI marketplace through such chicanery. He wanted the Chinese market, too. But since the U.S. and China are economic rivals, selling Nvidia’s wares to the People’s Republic of China was a bit of a no-no. Now, Huang did a bit of ring-kissing at the White House to get official approval to do business across the Pacific. But Huang appears to have done a bit of illicit, and mildly erotic, back-channeling to enter the Chinese market before getting that blessing.

Article continues below this ad

This is where a woman named Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen) enters the picture.

The honeypot. Huang is a managing director at a Singapore-based tech firm called Megaspeed. According to indispensable tech blogger Ed Zitron, in 2023 Megaspeed launched a subsidiary company named SpeedMatrix, which then purchased over $4 billion in Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs). The facts get murky from here, but the suspicion is that those GPUs were then smuggled into China. Meantime, Huang and Huang reportedly decide to mix business with pleasure. This was a bad move on Jensen Huang’s part, as he’s already a married man. Even thornier, the New York Times reported that as early as a year ago, U.S. lawmakers had reason to believe that Alice Huang was an operative for the Chinese government, had been working to evade U.S. export controls, and had developed a “close relationship” with Jensen Huang. With access to Nvidia’s advanced chips, China could pose an even larger security threat to the U.S. Mission accomplished, ma’am.

Q: Do we think the sex was good?It better have been.

Article continues below this ad

Q: What’s the fallout been?Still ongoing. Huang issued the standard public apology to his wife and kids, writing in a statement published Sunday, “I was unfaithful to my wife,” although he did not specify whom he had an affair with (if I were Lori Mills, the wife, I’d take his ass to the cleaners). The company also announced its own internal investigation. Meantime, someone in President Lame Duck’s administration may have deliberately quashed a federal investigation into Megaspeed that could have given us a clearer picture of the f—kery at hand. And the president himself, no stranger to using his penis in malevolent fashion, came to his new best buddy’s defense: “He had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy. And I really believe him.” If you share a taco salad with Trump and say nice things about him, he’ll believe anything you say.

Q: Do you think Huang was duped?In my opinion, it doesn’t matter. Whether or not Huang deliberately conspired with the Chinese or was an unwitting abettor, he’s still guilty as all hell. But don’t worry. Trump has already informed the nation that the FBI will be investigating the matter further.

The same. Trump already told Huang that he has nothing to fear from Patel’s FBI. So that was a fun waste of all of our time.

Article continues below this ad

Q: What does this mean for me?If you hold Nvidia stock (DISCLOSURE: My wife and I own some of this stock as part of our retirement nest egg), you’re probably not too happy about Jensen Huang’s dalliances. Since news of his possible entrapment broke in October, the company stock price has cratered from a high of $243.37 a share to, as of this writing, $168.18. Even worse, the company’s stranglehold on AI hardware threatens to hurt the value of every other major tech company, because all of these corporations have invested literal trillions of dollars into AI. If those companies tank, then suddenly there goes a hefty portion of your 401(k), your IRA, your pension, your everything.You are not alone. Nvidia shareholders are filing lawsuits against Huang, and Democrats poised to take control of the federal government after the New Year are sure to conduct a much more thorough inquiry into the saga than sorry-ass Kash Patel will. Also, even though Huang is the CEO of Nvidia, he, unlike the likes of Elon Musk, does not hold enough personal stake in his company to block Nvidia’s board from removing him. He can be fired. The problem is that no one at his company seems all that keen on pulling the trigger. Huang’s cult of personality at Nvidia is so strong that no one else there appears to believe that it can survive without him. And if that’s truly the case, do you guys REALLY want the second largest company in America to go down? Because there’s a chance that the implications from its demise could reverberate down to you, even if you don’t own any stock of any sort. Trump may be done and dusted, but the too-big-to-fail dilemma here in America is not. In other words, Huang is probably gonna get away with it.

Q: I hate this man! And his penis!So do I, my friend. So do I.

items.title: Steve Hilton is convinced he's going to win. Hahahaha.
items.content:
There’s a midterm election coming on Nov. 3, which includes a race here in California to determine who will replace Gov. Gavin Newsom. On the blue side of the ticket is unremarkable Democrat Xavier Becerra, whose chief positive attribute is that he is not a Republican. On the red side is Steve Hilton, an immigrant from the U.K. who gained U.S. citizenship in 2021. Hilton’s most high-profile political experience came back in the early 2010s, when he served as an adviser to then-U.K. prime minister and alleged porcine enthusiast David Cameron. But that experience, plus a lengthy stint as a commentator for Fox News, was enough to convince Hilton that he not only should run for governor, but that he WILL be the state’s next governor.

On the surface, he makes for an attractive candidate. Hilton is good company, and when I met him, he was as good at explaining the issues, as you would expect a seasoned broadcaster to be. He’s even reaching out to the gay community, albeit in somewhat awkward fashion. Listen to the man talk and you might come away thinking he’s a Democrat.

But Steve Hilton is not a Democrat. He’s a Republican, one who plans to give tax breaks to the wealthy, massively increase funding to the police and let artificial intelligence companies do basically whatever they want without fear of California regulation. Most importantly to me, he is backed by President and aspiring dictator Donald Trump. So, Hilton can’t run as a Republican, especially not in a state as firmly blue as California, without having to answer for that party’s standard-bearer. But God bless Hilton, he gave it a try, repeatedly, when I met with him in August. This was true right from my opening question, when I asked him why he wanted to run for governor here at all.

Article continues below this ad

“I love California and it’s obviously not working,” he told me. “Sixteen years of one-party rule, it’s a disaster. So we’ve got to turn things around.”

“OK,” I shot back, “but why would I trust a Republican to change any of this, in this administration?”

At this, Hilton feigned ignorance. “In which administration?”

Article continues below this ad

“The Trump 2 administration.”

“I don’t see the relevance of that to California.”

Hilton acknowledged none of those things. Instead, he continually portrayed himself as a heroic outsider. “I’m not the president,” he insisted, with a showman’s vigor. “I’m not him. I’m me.”

Article continues below this ad

When I brought up the president later in our conversation, he complained to me, “I don’t know why you keep talking about Trump.”

“That’s why I’m here,” I told him. “Because you’re a Republican. I want you to explain to me how you could possibly exist as a functional Republican with the standard-bearer of that party exercising a ridiculous amount of influence over the party and being a general, omniscient presence over the entire country, California included.”

“Well, I think that description, it just doesn’t match the facts,” Hilton told me. The polls at the time implied that voters did not agree. When I met Hilton in August, he was trailing Becerra badly, so I asked him why he was running a campaign that was doomed to fail. 

“That gap [in the polls] is shrinking,” he said to me, with no lack of confidence. “The gap went from 25 to 18 in the Berkeley poll. What was the next one? Our own internal poll, down to 14 points. There’s a poll that we’re hearing about next week where the gap will be under 10%.” 

Article continues below this ad

Hilton didn’t mention that he was quoting polls from before and after the primary, and the gap fell from 21 not 25, which is VERY much a Republican thing for him to do, but I still gave him the benefit of the doubt.

“Let’s say the poll numbers hold and you don’t win the election,” I said to him. “Where would you go after this?”

At this, he laughed. “I don’t know. I haven’t thought about it. I’m planning to win. I do believe that I’m going to be the next governor. I can see it. I believe it.”

Article continues below this ad

“Is that your ego talking? Have you convinced yourself?”

“No, it’s California talking. It’s the conditions in our state.”

“It’s not the polls talking.”

“Yes, but we’re just at the start of the campaign. No one really pays attention until after Labor Day anyway. Everything points to this being a change election in California. That means that I will win the election. That is my strong expectation.”

Article continues below this ad

But that confidence only holds if Hilton pretends the Trump factor in this race isn’t significant. Surely the voters he’d met along the trail had told him as much. That’s why I asked him, “Have you not had voters talk to you specifically about what the president is doing?”

That answer floored me. “Never?”

Article continues below this ad

“Literally never comes up,” Hilton boasted. “It’s ‘What are we going to do about the gas prices?’ Right now in California, you’ll see gas prices in the $5 to $6 range. If you go to Texas today, they’re in the $3 range. Same country, same president, same Iran war going on, vastly different gas prices. That’s entirely due to the policies that Democrats have pursued in California.”

He’s partially correct, given that California’s gas prices are high partially because the state has the highest gas tax in the country, and its fuel standards increase costs for producers. But he again fails to acknowledge the role the Trump administration has played in driving up prices nationwide. It’s a form of denial that he’s shown many times over, from asking voters to ignore Trump’s endorsement of him after he accepted it, to attempting to soften his affection for other members of the MAGA herd, including the late Charlie Kirk. Hilton came to our meeting sporting a wristband honoring the fallen white supremacist. I asked him why he had it.

“He was a good friend of mine, and someone gave it to me,” Hilton said about that. “So I just kept it.”

Article continues below this ad

“Did you like his way of going about things, because he was rather open about his views on race.”

“I’m not sure what you’re referring to.”

“Well, he was a friend of mine. I’m sure we all agree that we are friends with many people. That doesn’t mean we agree with 100% of everything they’ve ever said or done. You can still be friends with someone, just as I am with many Democrats. Don’t agree with them, but we’re friends.”

Article continues below this ad

Do not count Becerra, the Democratic candidate, as one such friend. Hilton made sure to get in his jabs at Becerra in between all of my nagging questions. “We haven’t even talked about all the disqualifying factors for my opponent, who, in the words of [former Biden official] Susan Rice is ‘an idiot.’ You can’t have an idiot as governor of California.” 

I asked if he thought Becerra was especially idiotic given the current level of stupidity in the Trump administration, but he quickly sidestepped. 

“I don’t know. You’d have to ask Susan Rice. I don’t know why she called him an idiot.”

Article continues below this ad

“Well, you just said it was a great quote about him, so you must think he’s an idiot, too.”

“I’m just telling you what people who have experience of working with him say. She also called him a ‘bitch-ass,’ whatever that means exactly.”

“I think you know what a bitch-ass means.”

“I actually, truly don’t know exactly what that means.”

Article continues below this ad

He must have learned in the interim. Because one week ago, Hilton faced off against Becerra in the only televised gubernatorial debate prior to the election. There, he brought up the “bitch-ass” comment from Rice directly to his opponent. He also constantly took umbrage anytime Becerra tried to link him to the president.

“All you ever say is ‘Trump, Trump, Trump,’” he admonished Becerra. “That’s nothing but an insult to every Californian who is desperate for something to change in this state.”

Article continues below this ad

If voters here are desperate for a change, they’re not buying Hilton as the face of it. Two weeks after Labor Day, he is now down against Becerra by 25 points. I don’t think he’s going to win this election. Because when you’re a Republican, there’s no hiding it.

items.title: I've got some demands for our new woke overlords
items.content:
Joy. Joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy joy.

Can you feel the joy, dear reader? I can. Tuesday night, voters nationwide handed the Democratic Party decisive power in both chambers of Congress. Democrats won in California, as they always do. But they also won in Michigan, and Georgia, and Wisconsin, and Texas. They might even win in Mississippi once all of the ballots are tallied. Mississippi! I didn’t even know they HAD voting in Mississippi! Holy crap! I wanna kiss all of you on the mouth, I’m so happy!

Now, what happened Tuesday night doesn’t automatically correct everything that’s happened over the past decade and beyond. You and I will still have to call out the usual suspects whenever the Democratic establishment gives into its eternally timid instincts. Some of those party regulars have already pre-caved. But that’s for another day. Regardless, today is for joy. Today is for you and I to pop bubbly with breakfast and hold our middle fingers aloft at the lame, overweight duck in the White House. Today is a day for celebration.

Article continues below this ad

In that spirit, I’ve cobbled together a quick to-do list for our new blue majority government. I bring you these demands as a voter, not a political analyst. Do not expect me to outline how I want all of the following things accomplished. That’s not my problem, Democrats. Figuring out the how of things is what I and my fellow taxpayers are paying you to sort out. I never want you to tell me why you do something anymore. Not after we just colonized Texas … emphatically.

Like Jon Rosenthal — the Democrat who just kicked a bigoted cowboy’s ass to win a seat on the Texas Railroad Commission — I’m feeling myself this morning. I was a VERY good voter this year, blue Santa Claus. Most of us were. Therefore, you’re gonna have to bring us everything that’s on our wish list, which I’ve written down below in loose priority order.

Nothing about Tuesday night will amount to anything as long as President Trump can go running to his lackeys on the bench to overturn any new law he dislikes, to suddenly legalize sexual assault, or to magically bestow upon Trump the power of wingless flight. I am sick to death of SCOTUS being the most actively malevolent political force in this supposedly free country. So first things first: Fix it. Again, the how is your problem, Dems. Not mine. If it means expanding the court to 24 judges, College Football Playoff-style, do it. If it means instituting term limits, so that an allegedly handsy fossil like Clarence Thomas can’t rule over our lives for and counting, do it. Or if it means impeaching evidentially corrupt justices like Thomas and the dreaded Sammy Alito, do that too. Speaking of which … 

Article continues below this ad

You and I have already endured two failed impeachment attempts on President Stands Weird, so I understand why you might groan at anyone who tells you that the third time will be the charm. But America can’t have a functional government if our new woke overlords allow proven criminals to get away with their evildoing. You saw Tuesday night’s returns. That wasn’t voters saying, “Maybe we should go easy on dear old Donald.” That was America screaming, “WE WANT BLOOD.”

Because Trump has presided over a still ongoing crime spree at the highest level of government, and the only way to prevent him and future leaders from committing more atrocities is to, you know, prosecute them. All of them. Not just Trump. I want the hammer to also fall on Alito, on Thomas, on Elon, on that zooted-up scumbag Pete Hegseth, and — well, look, it’s a long list and the internet only has so much memory storage. Even with all those shiny new data centers going up, there’s still not enough room for me to name every name. But you get the idea.

Article continues below this ad

Would you like to know why, on an otherwise lovely night, Californians rejected a tax on the state’s billionaires? Or how the discourse around the Michigan Senate race got sidetracked by Israel, which is not in Michigan? Through the magic of donations, that’s how. Ever since the Supreme Court — there those bastards are again — decided in 2010 that campaign finance restrictions were somehow a violation of free speech, the American political system has been wholly captured by big-money interests, from Israel to Mark Zuckerberg. Last year, a trio of Democrats proposed an amendment to overturn this disastrous SCOTUS decision. If they can get this amendment through with a majority now, it will end the essentially legalized bribery that has poisoned all political parties this century. That might give America the chance to be an actual democracy again.

Tell ’em, Peggy Flanagan:

I don’t want a kinder, gentler ICE. I don’t want a better-trained ICE. I want ICE, and I want any ICE goons who killed innocent people to be put in the slammer. Again, we can’t move forward as a country if we don’t hold the bad guys accountable. And we know who the bad guys are, because they all have X accounts where they confess on a daily basis. Time to put them out of commission.

Article continues below this ad

It was an illegal war from the very outset, and it has accomplished less than nothing. So let’s take the war keys away from Trump and give him a Whoozit to play with instead. Listen to how it squeaks, Mister President! They’re saying it’s the greatest toy ever invented!

I’m a 50-year-old man, and even wanna get an abortion now. I should have that right! After all, you never know!

I’m nursing a theory that Americans actually like monopolies because the board game taught them that monopolies are good. That is incorrect. I’d prefer there be MANY companies to get my news and entertainment from, instead of just one owned by some billionaire’s asshole kid. These monopolies are the reason why I need to take out a home equity loan just to afford my groceries. If Democrats really care about affordability, as they claim, breaking up the big boys is the first step.

Their product is crap, it eats up generations’ worth of energy, and it doesn’t make any money! So I don’t wanna hear about how we have to bail out Sam Altman and OpenAI to the tune of literal trillions because we might lose 300 jobs or whatever if they go bust. I’d rather that money be used toward far more promising endeavors, like:

Article continues below this ad

That includes abortions, and not just boner pills!

I wanna ride more choo choo trains!

Or pay my ass to stay home and raise these little bastards myself!

Article continues below this ad

Make NFL Sunday Ticket free! That one’s just for me, really.

Clean up Washington, D.C.! I mean this in the literal sense. Even if you live far away from the nation’s capital, you’re likely aware of the myriad ways in which Trump has desecrated it. He destroyed the Reflecting Pool. He destroyed the Kennedy Center. He destroyed a local public golf course. He’s destroying whatever portions of the Smithsonian he finds distasteful. And, of course, he’s bulldozed the East Wing of the White House in order to build a ballroom/war bunker/casino/Best Buy outlet. Just as you and I are represented by the people working in D.C., we’re also represented by the physical landscape of D.C. itself: the buildings, the museums, the monuments … all of it. The ruined D.C. that Trump is currently attempting to remodel in his bloated image is emblematic of the widespread damage he’s wrought on the nation itself. So please Democrats, give D.C. back to the American people. And don’t let Trump build that f—king arch. This is a celebration, and he’s not invited.

items.title: San Francisco's best hotel cannot be killed
items.content:
I am not a rock star, although I like to imagine myself as one. I imagine it so, so hard: packed stadiums, crowds numbering five figures going wild as I take my shirt off, shady managers hanging out backstage ready to ply me with Hefty bags full of pharmaceutical cocaine. But it’s too late for me, on the cusp of 50, to actually become a rock star — it certainly couldn’t be a skill or charisma issue, no sir — which is why there’s a tiny slice of the hospitality industry that exists to make patrons like me FEEL like rock stars, if only for a brief moment. 

This is where the legendary Phoenix Hotel, plopped down on Eddy Street right in the middle of San Francisco’s Tenderloin neighborhood, comes in.

I have stayed at many hotels in San Francisco, but all of them were hotels. Elevator banks. Free continental breakfast. A sad gym on the third floor where one treadmill is always busted. You know the kind of hotel I mean. The Phoenix, which opened in the 1980s at the influence of legendary rock promoter Bill Graham, is not that kind of hotel. This was a place dreamed up to serve real-deal rock stars, and to make anyone else staying there feel like part of the greater entourage.

Article continues below this ad

And until early this year, it was all set to die young, as so many of its more famous guests had, Kurt Cobain chief among them. Late in 2025, b. Patisserie co-owner Michel Suas was readying to take over the Phoenix’s lot and close down the hotel permanently, presumably using the land to build some kind of overpriced but good boulangerie. But at the last second, Suas had a change of heart! HONH HONH HONH! Enter local hotelier Binoy Patel, who took the reins of the property and is keeping the hotel open. That’s right, like a phoenix rising from the ashes. You read my mind to the letter.

Given this fortuitous stay of execution, my SFGATE bosses thought that I should stay at the Phoenix during my annual “Drew comes to the Bay Area for a weekand eatsway too much” trip two months ago. As a Marylander, I was ignorant to the Phoenix’s charms before booking my room. It is now my favorite hotel in the city, and if new owner Patel messes with so much as a single AC outlet in the place, he and I will have words.

I didn’t expect to love the Phoenix as much as I did, certainly not at first glance. No one stays in the Tenderloin for the Tenderloin. You stay in this part of town because you have some work engagement nearby. That’s why hotelier Chip Conley founded the hotel in the first place; it was close to venues where Graham booked gigs for headline acts. Otherwise, the place is located on a nondescript, run-down stretch of Eddy Street that’s a relative desert. The hotel itself is a refurbished roadside motel, the kind of place I’d normally expect to be murdered in. The only thing shielding your room door from the rest of the world is a red iron gate to the street next to the hotel office. So my first thought before ringing the front office door was, “This place better not suck.”

Article continues below this ad

I was buzzed by a clerk who bore more than passing resemblance to Sweetums the Muppet: a bulky, tatted-up fellow with long scraggy hair and the beard to match. Sweetums could have been the bouncer at a Hells Angels bar if he wasn’t such a sweetheart. Instead, he manned the front desk at the Phoenix and warmly offered me a number of vital pointers. I needed to use my key card at the red gate anytime I came or went, there was always free coffee in the front office if I needed it, and logging onto the hotel’s Wi-Fi required him to perform a live demo for me.

“I can’t do it the usual way?” I asked Sweetums.

“Doing it the usual way here is s—t,” he told me. But doing it his way worked like a charm.

Article continues below this ad

I walked into a concrete courtyard loosely festooned with palm trees, potted succulents, and basket chairs surrounding a fat round pool. An outdoor performance stage loomed toward the back. No one was swimming in the pool when I first entered the courtyard; the water was populated exclusively by aging pool noodles, some of which had bite marks in them. But the water looked clean, which is more than you can say for the average Motel 6 pool. I crossed the courtyard to the outdoor staircase leading up to my second floor room. Standing sentry by the staircase was a huge, colorfully tiled sculpture of a frog playing the guitar. Your mother would describe this hotel as “kind of funky,” and she’d be correct.

But the ultimate test for this kind of novelty hotel is your room itself. You want a hotel that’s only seedy. I’ve stayed at actual seedy hotels … the kind of hotels where s—t doesn’t work. They are not charming. So my room at the Phoenix would determine which side of the line the hotel fell on.

If you’ve read this far, you won’t be surprised to learn that my room was perfect. One side of it was dominated by a floor-to-ceiling window looking out onto the courtyard, just in case any other guests wanted to watch me and a groupie going at it. Seeing as how I’ve been faithfully married for 24 years, the chances of me indulging in that particular rock star fantasy were minimal. But it was nice to know I had the option if I so chose.

Article continues below this ad

As for the room itself, it had everything I would have wanted from a mainstream hotel room. The bed was comfy. There were multiple charging outlets available to me, many hidden inside of retro furnishings that scanned like film props. And I didn’t need a tutorial from Sweetums on how to operate the shower or the light switches. My only beef was that the soft neon lamp hanging over my bed didn’t work, but I probably wouldn’t have used it for longer than two minutes anyway.

This was a goodass hotel room, and it served as a perfect base of operations for me as I spent all week covering assignments in North Beach, Cow Hollow, Marin, Palo Alto, and elsewhere. Anytime I was slogging through my day of field reporting, I knew that my plush room at the Phoenix would be waiting for me. Best of all, when I asked Sweetums if there were any good places for breakfast nearby, he immediately told me to hit Brenda’s French Soul Food, another local institution I had been heretofore unaware of. I went to Brenda’s the following morning and ordered the bananas foster French toast, plus a breakfast sandwich. You know, for balance. I ate so well that brunch, I needed to burn some serious calories afterward.

And where better to do that than in the Phoenix pool?

Article continues below this ad

This was August, mind you. Temperatures in San Francisco that time of year aren’t always conducive to pool days, so I suited up with the mercury hovering around a crisp 65 in the hotel’s courtyard. I fully expected the water to be even colder than that, so imagine my surprise when I jumped off the edge and KERSPLOOSH! Suddenly I was warmer and happier than I’d been all trip. The Phoenix pool isn’t so hot as to feel gross, it’s just well calibrated for a warm swim in a city that wants you to slowly freeze to death. Once in the pool, I knew immediately that leaving the pool would render me a pile of chattering teeth. So I grabbed one of the chewed-up pool noodles and lounged to my big fat heart’s content.

I felt no danger from the dirty street outside, nor did I feel embarrassed to be a 49-year-old man, rash guard and all, swimming all by himself in the middle of a random weekday. I know that Sweetums was standing sentry at the front desk, and I knew that I was exactly where I wanted to be: kicking back in the heart of one of the best cities in the world, with not a single worry on my mind. If that’s not the life of a rock star, I don’t know what is.
